ego.name: Alan Turing
ego.summary: Alan Turing was an English mathematician, computer scientist, logician, cryptanalyst, and theoretical biologist. He formalized the concepts of algorithm and computation with the Turing machine, helped break German naval Enigma communications, and worked on early computers, artificial intelligence, and mathematical biology.

connections.relationship_description: Turing's mother helped arrange for him to be raised in England while she and Julius Turing worked in British India. She later published a biography of him.
Morcom was Turing's close friend at Sherborne School. They shared interests in mathematics and science until Morcom's death in 1930.
connections.notes: Turing remained in contact with Morcom's mother for many years after Morcom's death.

connections.relationship_description: Clarke was Turing's close friend and Hut 8 colleague. They became engaged in early 1941, but Turing ended the engagement after disclosing his homosexuality.
connections.notes: They remained close friends until Turing's death in 1954.

connections.relationship_description: Church supervised Turing's doctoral work at Princeton from 1936 to 1938. Turing completed Systems of Logic Based on Ordinals under his supervision.
connections.notes: Turing completed Systems of Logic Based on Ordinals under Church.

connections.relationship_description: Newman's Cambridge lectures on the foundations of mathematics helped inspire Turing's work on the Entscheidungsproblem. He recognized the importance of Turing's 1936 paper and later recruited him to Manchester.
connections.notes: Their relationship connected Turing's theoretical work on computation with postwar computer construction.

connections.relationship_description: Gandy worked with Turing on wartime speech-encryption methods and later completed a 1952 doctorate under Turing at Cambridge on axiomatic systems and theories in physics.
connections.notes: Gandy later became a major interpreter and editor of Turing's intellectual legacy.

connections.relationship_description: Knox worked with Turing on German Enigma cryptanalysis before and after Turing joined Bletchley Park in 1939.
connections.notes: Turing stayed with Knox and his wife in 1939 while consulting on Enigma work.

connections.relationship_description: Welchman and Turing were early Bletchley Park recruits, collaborated in the Enigma effort, and jointly signed the October 1941 appeal to Winston Churchill for more codebreaking resources.
connections.notes: Welchman's diagonal board complemented the British bombe program associated with Turing.

connections.relationship_description: Good served with Turing in Hut 8 on naval Enigma cryptanalysis and later worked with him at the University of Manchester on computers, statistics, and related problems.
connections.notes: Good's successful solution to a Hut 8 bigram-table problem won Turing's professional respect.

connections.relationship_description: Turing's father was an Indian Civil Service official whose work in British India led the parents to leave Alan and his brother in England for much of their childhood.
connections.notes: Julius and Ethel Turing arranged for their children to be raised in Britain while they traveled between Britain and India.

connections.relationship_description: Turing's elder brother shared the family's childhood arrangements in England while their parents worked in India.
After Christopher Morcom's death, Turing corresponded with Morcom's mother for years, including on anniversaries of her son's death.
connections.notes: Their correspondence records Turing's continuing grief and his commitment to the scientific interests he had shared with Christopher.

connections.relationship_description: Murray had a sexual relationship with Turing in 1951–1952; their association led to the police investigation and prosecution of both men for homosexual acts.
connections.notes: The prosecution had grave personal and professional consequences for Turing.

connections.relationship_description: Turing attended Wittgenstein's 1939 Cambridge lectures on the foundations of mathematics, where the two argued over formalism, mathematical truth, and computation.
connections.notes: Their recorded exchanges show a substantive disagreement between Turing's formalist outlook and Wittgenstein's philosophical approach.

connections.relationship_description: Besicovitch assessed Turing's dissertation for the King's College fellowship in 1935. He praised the originality of its mathematical methods.
connections.notes: His favorable report helped establish Turing as a Fellow of King's College, Cambridge.

connections.relationship_description: Michie and Turing worked together during the war on speech-encryption methods, including a machine code-named Delilah, before Michie became a leading British artificial-intelligence researcher.
Champernowne was Turing's friend from King's College, Cambridge, and worked with him in 1948 on Turochamp, an early chess-playing computer program.
connections.notes: Their collaboration linked Turing's interest in machine intelligence to a practical game-playing program.

category_summaries.summary: Julius and Ethel Turing worked in British India while Alan and John Turing were raised largely in England. Ethel Turing later published a biography of her son.

Turing’s personal relationships ran from Sherborne School to Bletchley Park and Manchester. Christopher Morcom shared his interest in mathematics and science until his death in 1930. Joan Clarke worked with Turing at Hut 8 and remained his friend after their engagement ended. Turing’s relationship with Arnold Murray led to the 1952 prosecution.

At Cambridge, Max Newman’s lectures introduced Turing to questions about the foundations of mathematics. Alonzo Church supervised Turing’s Princeton doctorate on ordinal logic. Turing later attended Ludwig Wittgenstein’s Cambridge lectures and argued with him about mathematics and computation. Robin Gandy carried forward work on logic after studying under Turing.

At Bletchley Park, Turing worked with codebreakers on German Enigma communications and naval cryptanalysis. After the war, work with colleagues in Manchester connected him to early stored-program computers and chess programming.
